title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Adjudication of Cases Involving Spousal Debt Disputes

articles.content_en: Article 1: Where a debt is incurred based on the mutual expression of intent such as both spouses jointly signing or one spouse subsequently ratifying it, such debt shall be recognized as a joint debt of the spouses.

Article 2: Where a debt is incurred by one spouse in his/her personal name during the existence of the marital relationship for the daily living needs of the family, and a creditor claims rights on the ground that the debt is a joint debt of the spouses, the People's Court shall support such claim.

Article 3: Where a debt is incurred by one spouse in his/her personal name during the existence of the marital relationship exceeding the daily living needs of the family, and a creditor claims rights on the ground that the debt is a joint debt of the spouses, the People's Court shall not support such claim, unless the creditor can prove that the debt was used for the joint living or joint production and operation of the spouses or was based on the mutual expression of intent of both spouses.

Article 4: This Interpretation shall come into force as of January 18, 2018.
After this Interpretation comes into force, if any relevant judicial interpretation previously made by the Supreme People's Court conflicts with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail.
